requirements.requirement: Kernel configured to boot with audit=1 (persistent bootloader configuration for all kernel entries)
requirements.summary: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX updated in /etc/default/grub and grubby --update-kernel=ALL applied audit=1 to both the default and rescue BLS kernel entries; grub2.cfg regenerated; grubby --info=ALL confirmed args include audit=1 for both kernels.

requirements.requirement: Setting takes effect on the running kernel after a reboot (actual verification, not just config)
requirements.summary: Boot identity changed from 55595e92-... to 669ea8e7-... across a real reboot, and the post-reboot live /proc/cmdline shows audit=1 appended, confirming the kernel actually booted with the parameter.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (not just the current boot)
requirements.summary: The change was made via persistent GRUB/BLS configuration (not a one-time kernel argument), and after the reboot the grub config and grubby --info for the default kernel still show audit=1, confirming it will apply on subsequent boots as well. Only one reboot cycle was directly observed.

requirements.requirement: System/service health maintained through the change (auditd and general node health before/after)
requirements.summary: auditd was active and enabled before the change and remained active/enabled after the reboot; no failed services appeared in before/after lifecycle snapshots.

overall_summary: The executor persistently configured audit=1 via /etc/default/grub and grubby --update-kernel=ALL across all BLS kernel entries, regenerated grub2.cfg, and performed a real, single-node reboot. Boot identity changed (55595e92... -> 669ea8e7...) and the post-reboot live /proc/cmdline confirms audit=1 is active on the running kernel. auditd remained healthy before and after, and grub config verification post-reboot confirms the setting remains in place for future boots. All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct before/during/after evidence.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was directly observed; persistence was inferred from bootloader config remaining set post-reboot rather than from a second independent reboot.
No corroborating audit log (e.g., ausearch/journal boot markers) was captured to independently confirm the audit subsystem behavior beyond auditctl -s and systemctl is-active.

operational_hygiene.summary: Commands were tightly scoped to the task: baseline capture (read-only), a backup of /etc/default/grub before editing (low-risk, retained but harmless), the grub/grubby config change itself, a single acknowledged reboot, and post-reboot verification. Lifecycle diff shows only expected reboot artifacts (new boot_id, new systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot, new sshd/chronyd PIDs) plus a small /tmp/reboot.log left from the backgrounded reboot command — a low-risk, directly reboot-attributable residue, not an unrelated mutation. No failed services, no unrelated package or network changes, no unnecessary experimentation observed in the 6-command timeline.
